A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ResAD and provide readable, matchable text, equations, figures and tables. Both end with references and contain no appendix; separately mentioned supplementary material is not included in either supplied PDF.

before.justification: V1 reports original NAVSIM v1/v2 evaluations, component ablations and transfer experiments in Tables 1–4, alongside qualitative results and training curves.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds runtime, multimodal-quality and inference-scaling results in Table 5 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the constant-velocity reference, residual normalization, Gaussian reference perturbations, diffusion objectives and trajectory ranker. Rewritten explanations and omitted implementation details do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate trajectory planning on NAVSIM v1 and v2 using the same NuPlan-derived coverage. The additional analyses concern existing driving coverage and inference configurations, without a documented new dataset, domain or test environment.

E2.justification: V2 adds DistillDrive to the NAVSIM v1 comparison in Table 1, reporting PDMS 86.2 with ResNet-34. Existing comparators remain, and Table 2's NAVSIM v2 comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols evaluate candidate-average PDMS, runtime and FPS at 20 inference candidates in Table 5, and sweep candidate counts from 8 to 256 in Figure 6. The primary splits, training budget, default 200 inference candidates and two denoising steps remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 substantially expands the analysis with residual-versus-reference case studies in Figure 5, computational cost and multimodal-quality comparisons in Table 5, and inference-sample sensitivity in Figure 6. The existing component ablations, transfer experiments and PRNorm training curves are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2's candidate-average PDMS measures multimodal output quality, rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises ResAD/ResNet-34 PDMS from 88.6 to 88.8, DAC from 97.3 to 97.5, EP from 82.5 to 83.3 and TTC from 94.2 to 94.1. Table 3 updates the final model but reports EP 83.4. Substantial new results include candidate-average PDMS of 86.1 versus DiffusionDrive's 60.3 at 20 candidates, and the inference-scaling curves. Table 4 is unchanged, but its prose is corrected from 85.4/85.9 to 85.2/85.6.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(15) and their mathematical assumptions are retained. Changing the clean-sample symbol from x0 to z0 corrects notation; no substantive derivation, theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion soften the claim that a counterfactual reference induces causal understanding, emphasizing instead a physical prior that simplifies learning context-dependent corrections. The central residual-modeling, normalization and state-of-the-art planning claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations of residual directions during cruising and maneuvers, low-cost integration into other planners, ranker overhead and inference scaling through context-constrained sampling. Section 4.4 still invokes a counterfactual interpretation despite the softened headline framing; no dedicated limitations discussion is added.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 removes the three-camera cropping/resizing and 1024-by-256 input description, LiDAR rasterization details, and ranker training with a fixed vocabulary and frozen diffusion model. V2 adds NVIDIA 4090 timing information and explicitly documents the V2-99 backbone already evaluated in v1. Code-release information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 substantially broadens the cited literature, adding works such as DriveLM, DiffVLA, Reason2Drive, R2P2, Trajectron++ and DistillDrive. These additions expand coverage of reasoning, generative planning and forecasting, while the principal contrast with direct trajectory prediction and static vocabularies remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, method explanations, quantitative discussion and conclusion receive extensive rewriting. Section 4.4 is reorganized into named analyses and a three-part discussion of advantages, while the main section order remains intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 5–6 and Table 5 within the retained visual structure. Existing displays largely persist, with revised captions, relocated Figure 4, publication labels in comparison tables and an additional Table 1 row; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Table 5 and Figure 6 provide useful quantitative support for multimodal quality and inference scaling beyond v1's largely qualitative discussion. V2 also moderates headline causal claims and corrects the Table 4 prose. These gains modestly improve the paper, but are tempered by removed preprocessing and ranker-training details and the new EP discrepancy between Tables 1 and 3.
